Q1: What should this heal issue (target `main`) change, given that the resolver's refusal is an intentional security boundary?
Choices:
A) Change only the heal routing. When an `autofix_failure` report's reason is a non-retryable sandbox-path reason (`conflict_resolver_sandbox_path_host_only`, etc.), the intake files no heal issue (no new `workflow-defect` / `inconclusive` issues). Instead it asks a human to merge the named host-only paths on the source PR. Add a regression test that feeds this report to the intake and fails on today's routing. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Add a deterministic host-side resolution. When the live `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` conflicts and its `workflow-templates/` twin resolves cleanly, copy the twin over the live copy before the conflicted-path check. **Note:** this lets content the model resolved reach a host-executed safety hook, which loosens the boundary the fix constraints say must not be weakened.
C) Make no shared-code change. Close this issue as "no shared-code defect", and a human merges PR #6535's hook conflict on `ai/issue-6525` by hand.
Q2: If Q1 = A, how should the human hand-off be shown? (Ignore this if Q1 is B or C.)
Choices:
A) Label the source PR `ai:needs-human`. Post one comment on it naming the host-only paths with the existing `::error::` headline, and send a Telegram WARNING. Record it in the intake log as `WORKFLOW_HEAL skip reason=non_retryable_host_only` (a new reason value under the existing `WORKFLOW_HEAL` prefix). (RECOMMENDED)
B) Post the diagnosis comment on the PR (the existing `pr-self-inflicted` path), but add no label and send no Telegram alert.
C) Classify the report as `consumer-config` (Telegram plus a comment only, as the intake already does for that class), with no label.
